Question B-005-010-009.

Why the correct answer is right: At audio frequencies, a suitably chosen radio-frequency bypass capacitor has high reactance. That keeps it from shunting much wanted audio signal.

Why the distractors are wrong:
- sourceIndex 1: "Low reactance at radio frequencies": Low radio-frequency reactance explains why RF can be bypassed. It does not explain why the audio circuit is little affected.
- sourceIndex 2: "High reactance at radio frequencies": High RF reactance would make the part a poor RF bypass capacitor.
- sourceIndex 3: "Low reactance at audio frequencies": Low audio reactance would load or short the audio signal, so the audio circuit would be affected.
